In a lengthy interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses recent changes to the company's ChatGPT desktop app and outlines plans to eventually eliminate the tabbed interface. Watch the video below.

Work features will eventually work seamlessly within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Stern previewed the upcoming interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand-new YouTube channel, New Things.

Stern published the full interview today, covering topics including the new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware development plans, a lawsuit against Apple, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern brought up OpenAI's recent decision to merge its ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, while also introducing a new agent mode for ChatGPT called Work.

The merged interface left users confused—particularly those who just wanted to keep using ChatGPT and were struggling to find their conversations.

OpenAI has since updated the app, adding separate tabs at the top for Work and ChatGPT, and a sidebar dropdown for switching between ChatGPT and Codex. It's slightly easier to use, but the interface remains a bit complex overall.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, acknowledging the new interface was "indeed a bit messy," but added that it was a "transitional step" toward the future, in which the Work tab will disappear and its features will be "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also noted that despite the chaos surrounding the merged app's launch, OpenAI has already seen the intended effect: Codex's user base doubled from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

Pressed on whether the growth was simply a result of bundling Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman conceded once again, but argued that, in a sense, that was exactly the effect they expected to achieve:
